appearance.twig.note: Sargent's Manual (2nd ed. 1922, read at the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17), as Alnus rubra: "slender branchlets marked by minute scattered pale lenticels, light green and coated at first with hoary tomentum ..., becoming during the first winter bright red and lustrous and ultimately ashy gray". Colour chosen by eye for the red of twigs past their first summer, which carry most of a crown's twig wood.

traits.shade_tolerance.note: FEIS's red alder review (Alnus rubra, read 2026-10-16): "Due to red alder's shade intolerance, stands are self-thinning"; its rapid juvenile growth gives "the shade-intolerant red alder" its edge over conifers.

traits.flowering_months.note: FEIS (Alnus rubra): in Oregon and Washington it flowers from late February to early May. Too few iNaturalist records in the Puget Sound lowlands are annotated as flowering to count (22).

traits.fruiting_months.note: FEIS (Alnus rubra): fruit ripe from early August to late October at 17 places in Oregon and Washington. Its seed is shed through the fall and winter, and old cones hang on longer still (USA-NPN observers see ripe fruit on it in every month), but a season holds one year from its February buds, so only the ripening months are stated.

traits.height_max_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923), as Alnus oregona: grows 15 m to 25 m tall.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923), as Alnus oregona: leaves 7 cm to 12 cm long.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923), as Alnus oregona: petioles 15-20 mm long.

traits.wood_modulus_green_mpa.note: Wood Handbook 2021 (FPL-GTR-282), table 5-3a, Alder, red, green: modulus of elasticity 8,100 MPa in static bending (clear wood, centre-loaded, span 14 depths; specific gravity 0.37).

traits.wood_rupture_green_mpa.note: Wood Handbook 2021 (FPL-GTR-282), table 5-3a, Alder, red, green: modulus of rupture 45,000 kPa (clear wood in static bending).

traits.wood_moisture_green_share.note: Wood Handbook 2021 (FPL-GTR-282), table 4-1, Alder, red: average moisture content of green wood, sapwood 97% of oven-dry mass; stated as a share, the range between them with its middle typical where both are given.

traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 species aggregate for Alnus rubra (gwddagg_v2.2_species.csv, read): specific gravity 0.41 (wsg_est, the database's hierarchical-model species mean, from 5 records in 3 sources); trunks 0.41, branches 0.45. Basic density (oven-dry mass over green volume) is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

generator.params.path_half.note: A choice of the model's (crown form step B, broadleaf revision 11): the wood from the base at which a shoot's nodes are half as long, fitted so the plant grows to the height of its oldest reference size, with the crown's width left to grow inside the loose region.

generator.params.pipe_tip.note: A choice of the model's (crown form step B): the twig's and the leaf's pipe radii are scaled together so the stem's diameter at breast height matches the oldest reference size; the fuller crowns of broadleaf revision 11 carry more leaf, so the yearly rings (pipe_rings) are fitted near zero and the pipe model sets the diameter.

traits.juvenile_period_years.note: The Woody Plant Seed Manual (Alnus, table 3, read): minimum seed-bearing age 3 to 4 years. FEIS (Uchytil 1989, read): seed production begins at about 10 years, but sometimes sooner. It sets adult_age through the rule at the seed plants (spec rework P6), in place of the 6 years set by hand.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a fast-growing tree with a straight stem, a narrow, rounded crown, alternate oval leaves with double-toothed edges, and hanging catkins. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 15 m tall and 22 cm across at breast height at 20 years in the open; 24 m tall and 40 cm across at breast height at 40 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: dark green leaves; smooth, pale grey bark, often blotched with lichen. Fruit (plant roadmap P4), as in mid-July: small green cones (strobiles) about 2 cm long, three to eight on a short raceme. Its year (appearance.organs.bloom.season) takes its days of bud, flower, fruit, ripe and fall from the months it flowers and fruits in, by the rules at the flowering plants (development, 2026-10-14); until then they were authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands: catkins in February; the cones green through the summer, brown from September, hanging on into the next winter. The forest's packages show day 196 (mid-July) until the phenology of plant roadmap P5 sets the day from the date and the local climate. Bark pattern (plant roadmap P4, `bark_pattern`): smooth thin grey bark, whitened in patches by lichens, with lenticels; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Leaf families (plant roadmap P4, `families`): sun leaves somewhat smaller and narrower than shade leaves; set from general knowledge of sun and shade leaves and juvenile foliage, not measured.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy from the step-6 catalogue, authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands. Calibration against measurements and photographs is milestone P4.
